title: Kindle vs Kindle Paperwhite: is it worth paying more in 2026?
description: Kindle vs Kindle Paperwhite compared on screen, light, waterproofing, battery and weight, with today's UK prices and the one to buy.
intro:

Prices checked at Argos and John Lewis on 14 November 2026, and the Signature Edition again on PriceSpy on 16 November, when Amazon's own Kindle deals started. Black Friday is on 27 November, so we'll update this page as prices change.

body:
## The short answer

The basic Kindle is a very good e-reader, and at £84.99 it's the cheapest way into Kindle books. The Paperwhite costs more but fixes the three things people notice after a few weeks: the small 6-inch screen, no waterproofing and no warm light for reading in bed. If you read most nights, the Paperwhite is worth the extra. If you read on holiday and the odd commute, the basic Kindle is enough.

The twist this week is that the **Paperwhite Signature Edition is cheaper than the standard Paperwhite**. John Lewis has the Signature at £139.99, while the standard 16GB Paperwhite is £184.99 at John Lewis and Argos. So right now the choice is really basic Kindle at £84.99 or Signature at £139.99.

## Kindle vs Kindle Paperwhite: the differences that matter

These are the 2024 models, which are what most UK shops still stock. Specs are from the retailers' listings.

- **Screen:** Kindle 6 inches; Paperwhite 7 inches. Both are 300ppi, so text is equally sharp. The extra inch means fewer page turns and more room for bigger fonts.
- **Waterproofing:** Kindle none; Paperwhite waterproof. That matters for the bath, the beach and the pool.
- **Warm light:** Kindle has a plain white front light; Paperwhite lets you shift from white to amber, which is easier on the eyes late at night.
- **Battery:** Kindle up to 6 weeks; Paperwhite up to 12 weeks. Both charge by USB-C.
- **Weight:** Kindle 158g; Paperwhite 214g. The basic Kindle is noticeably lighter and fits a coat pocket.
- **Storage:** both 16GB, which holds thousands of books. The Signature Edition has 32GB, which only matters if you load up on audiobooks.
- **Price:** £84.99 vs £184.99 today, or £139.99 for the Signature.

What they share: the same Kindle store, the same e-ink screen type, no glare in sunlight, Audible playback over Bluetooth, and Kindle Unlimited support.

## What does the Signature Edition add?

The Signature Edition is a Paperwhite with three extras: an auto-adjusting front light that changes brightness as the room gets darker, wireless charging (the dock is sold separately), and 32GB of storage. It also comes without lock-screen ads. None of those is essential, but at £139.99 it costs £45 less than the standard Paperwhite, so there's no reason to buy the cheaper-spec model at full price this week.

## Which Kindle should you buy?

**Buy the basic Kindle if** you read a book a month or so, mainly at home or on trains, and want the lightest, cheapest option. It's also the better choice for older children, though the Kindle Kids version adds a case and a two-year guarantee.

**Buy the Paperwhite (Signature) if** you read daily, read in the bath or on holiday, or read in bed next to someone who's trying to sleep. The warm light and bigger screen make long sessions more comfortable.

**Skip the Colorsoft** unless you read comics, graphic novels or cookbooks. Colour doesn't help with novels, and the 16GB Colorsoft is £239.99 at John Lewis.

## Ads or no ads?

Kindles sold "with special offers" show ads on the lock screen and home screen, never inside books. You can remove them later for a one-off fee. The cheap prices above are for the ad-supported basic Kindle and standard Paperwhite. The Signature Edition doesn't have ads.

## Good prices to aim for

- **Kindle (2024, 16GB):** £84.99 is a good price. Last Black Friday it reached £69.99.
- **Kindle Paperwhite (2024, 16GB):** don't pay £184.99. It fell to £134.99 last Black Friday, so aim for under £140.
- **Paperwhite Signature Edition (2024, 32GB):** £139.99 is the lowest we've seen. Buy at this price.

Amazon discounts its own devices every Black Friday (27 November 2026), and the deals usually start in the week before. Amazon is also rolling out refreshed 2026 models, which tends to push the older generation down. See our [Kindle Black Friday deals guide](/guides/kindle-black-friday-deals-2026/) for the new range, and [every Black Friday 2026 guide](/black-friday/) for other brands. If it's a present, it's also in our [Christmas gift guides](/christmas-gifts/).

### Is the Kindle Paperwhite worth it over the basic Kindle?

For regular readers, yes. The bigger screen, warm light and waterproofing make a real difference for daily use. If you read occasionally, the basic Kindle does the same job for less.

### Is the basic Kindle screen as sharp as the Paperwhite?

Yes. Both have 300ppi screens, so text looks equally crisp. The Paperwhite's screen is bigger, not sharper.

### Can you read Kindle books without a Kindle?

Yes. The free Kindle app works on phones, tablets and computers, so try that first if you're unsure. An e-reader is easier on the eyes and the battery lasts weeks.

### Do you need Kindle Unlimited?

No. You can buy books one at a time. Kindle Unlimited is a monthly subscription for a large catalogue of mostly smaller-publisher titles. Our [Kindle Unlimited free trial guide](/guides/kindle-unlimited-free-trial-uk/) explains whether it's worth it.

### Where's cheapest for Kindles?

Amazon usually sets the price and Argos, Currys and John Lewis match it. This week John Lewis has price-matched the basic Kindle at £84.99, the same as Argos.
